disputes.description: All eight bodies are byte-identical one-line forwards `return StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(a1);` (sub_499E40..0x49AD50, 0x4A1EA0) or `ShortComputation_1b70(this)` tail calls. The distinct behavioral claims in the names (path registry vs single call vs delegation vs triple dispatch vs reverse dynamics) are NOT supported by the raw C bodies; treat as heuristic, not evidence of distinct behavior.
Misleading: the body copies a3 into a 68-byte stack struct (v6[64]=1, v7=0) and forwards to sub_4A2010 PitCrewMeshLoader; there is no reversed string copy.
Misleading: the body frees four linked lists (next pointer at node+0x44) via FreeWrapper_7bcf; there is no arithmetic comparison anywhere.
Name is behaviorally plausible (mesh resource load into a node list) but 'pit crew' is not derivable from this packet's raw C alone; no caller or string in this packet ties the mesh to pit crew.
The body does load BMPs and populate lookup fields on an init-once-guarded object, so 'dashboard setup' is plausible, but 'LED gauge' specifics are not visible in the raw C; partial over-claim.
The thunk forwards (this, a2) to StringCopyWithBufferRealloc; the target-name in the filename is an unresolved symbol guess, not evidence the callee address 0x566650 owns the string copy behavior.

unresolved: Cluster granularity: this packet mixes pure string-registration forwards, content loaders (bitmaps, gauges, mesh), container constructors/teardowns, and two game-state dispatch steps. One cluster-level lifecycle contract is proposed, but a finer split (interface kind for the registration forwards, type kind for mesh_container/cockpit_dashboard) is likely needed at reconciliation.

No single function is the cluster entry point; sub_4A00A0 is used as the representative signature because it is the largest and drives the session/content step, but the packet provides no caller evidence proving it is the entry.

StringCopyWithBufferRealloc ABI: the thiscall thunk sub_49A2C0 passes (this, a2) while the stdcall forwards pass a single a1. Whether the single-arg wrappers pass the string as `this` with an implicit second argument, or the decompiler collapsed an argument, is unresolved without the callee (out of packet).
The 40-byte objects in dword_7CE23C (constructed by ShortComputation_cb70) have no in-packet field layout; only the 4-slot pointer array at 0x7CE23C is evidenced.
cockpit_dashboard+0x04..0x18 / +0x20..0x48 field semantics depend on out-of-packet types (StringSearchInLinkedList and sub_548890 lookups); only the writes are evidenced, not the value meanings.

sub_49CD80 reads callee-defined structs: content_node+0x54 (node resource ptr), gauge_asset+0x1C/+0x20 floats, audio node +0x54, and its a1 base (cockpit_dashboard+0x60.. stride 0x4C); their full layout is outside the packet.

mesh_container+0x64 is written as the node-list head by sub_4A2010 (via MeshResourceAllocator / *v7) but read as a 3D sound source by sub_4A2220 (F_3DSoundSourceDestructor): same offset, possibly a union or a shared pointer slot; rule-9 forbids claiming shared ownership between the two functions.
mesh_container+0x04 is both the strcpy'd mesh-name string (sub_4A2010) and a single-byte write (sub_4A2220); recorded at width 1, but the exact string-buffer width/length is unresolved.
sub_4A1F60 (16-byte zero) and sub_4A1FB0 (28-byte init, +0x18=24) share the zero-write pattern but no caller or layout proves a common type; kept as separate objects.
sub_4A00A0's state gating constants (dword_7D0410==4, dword_7C56A4==7, dword_7D032C==1) and the dword_7C54E8+0x32E0/+0x344C field accesses depend on out-of-packet session/vehicle types.
sub_4A0490 case-4 content-path strings (dword_7CE630, v2+47) and the virtual call on dword_5EB10C vtable+0x0C are only partially resolvable without those callees.
sub_4A1EC0's literals asc_5CD148/asc_5CD144 and the sub_5665B0 behavior are opaque; 'settings path' framing in the filename is plausible but unverified.

String literal content behind IDA symbols (aVehicledisplay, aNetproblemBmp, aNexttrackBmp, aNextsessionBmp, aCmapsMas, aFiashortBik, aMainMenu, aCubeErrorLoadi, aDDevF119992002_2) is not visible in the packet's raw C; only the symbol names are evidenced.
